Absolute vs Gauge Pressure: Quick Conversion Table

Absolute vs gauge pressure differ only in the zero reference. Absolute pressure is measured from a perfect vacuum, while gauge pressure is measured from the local atmospheric pressure. The link between them is always: absolute pressure = gauge pressure + atmospheric pressure.

PointAbsolute pressureGauge pressure
Zero referencePerfect vacuumLocal atmosphere
Unit suffixpsia, bar(a), kPa(a)psig, bar(g), kPa(g)
Reading open to air at sea levelAbout 14.7 psia or 1.013 bar(a)0 psig or 0 bar(g)
Can it be negative?No, lowest value is zeroYes, vacuum reads below zero
Effect of weather and altitudeNot affectedReading shifts with barometric pressure
Typical useVacuum systems, gas density and flow, boiling point workTanks, pipelines, pumps, tyres

Worked Conversions at Sea Level

  1. A line at 2 bar(g) is 2 + 1.013 = 3.013 bar(a).
  2. A vacuum vessel at minus 0.8 bar(g) is 1.013 minus 0.8 = 0.213 bar(a).
  3. A tyre at 34 psig is 34 + 14.7 = 48.7 psia.

At higher altitude the atmospheric value is lower, so use the local barometric pressure rather than the sea level figure when converting.
